lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.title: Sea Turtle Form & Flippers
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.summary: Build a three-quarter sea turtle by comparing shell, head and near/far flipper sizes, then add controlled shell structure.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.step.shell_: Build the shell as a tilted three-dimensional mass, then add a simple axis that shows its direction.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.help.shell_: Avoid a perfect circle. Let the shell stretch and turn along the axis.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.complete.sh: The shell now has a clear direction and proportion.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.step.head_n: Attach a smaller neck and head so they overlap the front edge of the shell.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.help.head_n: Compare sizes: the head should feel clearly smaller than the shell, but not tiny.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.complete.he: Good relative scale. The head connects naturally to the shell.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.step.near_f: Build larger near flippers and smaller far flippers, letting some shapes overlap the shell.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.help.near_f: Near forms can be broader. Far forms can be shorter and partly hidden.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.complete.ne: The size differences make the turtle feel three-dimensional.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.step.shell_: Add a controlled inner shell arc and a few cross lines that follow the shell form.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.help.shell_: Let the lines bend with the shell instead of drawing a flat grid.
lesson.sea_turtle_form_study.complete.sh: Your shell structure supports the form without covering it in decoration.
